text:
Alex G: heads up — I'm seeing a bunch of GPU inference pods land on the general-compute nodepool instead of the gpu-isolated-pool after last night's nodepool rollout.
Mira: really? any logs or pod examples?
Alex G: `kubectl get pods -o wide | grep inference` shows several inferences on nodes labeled `pool=general-compute` even though deployments have `tolerations: gpu=true:NoSchedule` and an affinity for `gpu=true`.
Simon: hmm, did we change any daemonsets or node labels during the rollout?
Alex G: yeah we rolled a logging agent daemonset that intentionally tolerates `gpu=true`. suspect it's triggering schedule collisions because the daemonset toleration makes nodes appear "compatible" to the scheduler and cluster-autoscaler then scales the wrong nodegroup.
Priya: can you paste a pod yaml excerpt?
Alex G: sure — snippet:
```
spec:
  tolerations:
  - key: "gpu"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "true"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
  nodeAffinity:
    requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      nodeSelectorTerms:
      - matchExpressions:
        - key: "pool"
          operator: "In"
          values: ["gpu-isolated-pool"]
```
Mira: that config looks fine, but if node labels got copied to wrong instance group or the autoscaler sees node taints differently it could pick the closest ASG with available capacity — which for us is general-compute.
infra-bot: [autoscaler] scaled up nodegroup general-compute-std-2 to 3 nodes (reason: insufficient resources for pods: gpu/1).
Alex G: exactly — autoscaler chose general-compute-std-2, it doesn't have the `gpu-isolated=true` label we expect, so pods landed there.
Simon: two separate issues: 1) our daemonset toleration is too broad, 2) autoscaler is using resource requests alone to pick nodegroup.
Priya: quick mitigation: can we patch the daemonset to add `tolerationSeconds` or narrow the key to `logging/gpu` so it doesn't advertise generic `gpu=true`?
Mira: +1. Also we should add a `nodeSelector` to inference deployment as short-term — forces scheduling to proper pool regardless of tolerations.
Alex G: trying patch now:
```
kubectl patch ds logging-agent -n infra --type json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/tolerations/0/key","value":"logging/gpu"}]'
```
infra-bot: [patch] logging-agent patched by Alex G (rollout in progress).
Alex G: also applied `nodeSelector: { pool: gpu-isolated-pool }` to the inference deployment to prevent further misplacement.
Priya: also we should update autoscaler config to prefer nodegroups with `pool=gpu-isolated-pool` label for GPU taints — there's a CA flag for balancing groups by label affinity, I'll open a PR.
Simon: long-term: remove daemonsets from having cluster-wide generic gpu tolerations, and switch to specific toleration keys + admission checks. Also add scheduler predicates: require explicit node label match for GPU workloads (`nodeAffinity` > required).
Mira: can we also add a validation webhook to detect pods with `tolerations` referencing generic `gpu` key unless they also have nodeSelector for gpu-isolated?
Priya: yes I'll prototype a policy in gatekeeper and add an alert if any pod without nodeSelector tolerates `gpu=true`.
Alex G: cost note — autoscaler scaled 2 extra general nodes (preemptible) and some jobs hit higher egress to those zones, we should reconcile cost impact after rollback.
Mira: thanks. next steps: Priya PR for autoscaler labels, Simon to audit daemonsets for tolerations, Alex to run rollout rollback if placements continue.
Simon: leaving a quick grep command for audit:
`kubectl get ds --all-namespaces -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.namespace}/{.metadata.name}: {.spec.template.spec.tolerations[*].key}
' | grep -i gpu`
Alex G: will run that and post results. thanks all :thumbsup:
